memos.headline: Rotation into Defensives and Cyclicals Accelerates as Mega-Cap Tech Breaks Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe: XOM, PG, and CAT are in powerful uptrends with strong relative strength versus SPY (+10-13% over 4 weeks, +13-30% over 12 weeks), while MSFT and AMZN are in confirmed downtrends well below both moving averages. XOM at 152.50 sits just 2% off its 52-week high with RSI 63.8—strong but not yet overbought—and CAT at 742.83 is up 78% over 26 weeks with RSI 57.9, though its 46.5% premium to the 200-day mean raises mean-reversion risk. PG's RSI of 72 is the only overbought reading in the group, but its low ATR of 1.94% and relentless relative strength (+12.7% vs SPY over 4 weeks) suggest a defensive bid that may persist. MSFT is the clearest avoid: down 27.5% from its high, 19% below its 200-day mean, RSI 36.4, and losing relative strength at an accelerating pace (-20.2% vs SPY over 12 weeks). I would need MSFT to reclaim 420 (roughly its 50-day mean) before reconsidering.

views.note: Near 52-week highs with +30% 12-week relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below 140.
Persistent defensive bid with +12.7% 4-week relative strength, though RSI 72 warrants tighter stops; invalidated below 158.
Massive uptrend (+78% in 26 weeks) with strong relative strength, but 46% above 200-day mean creates mean-reversion risk; would cut below 680.
Confirmed downtrend: 27.5% off highs, 19% below 200-day mean, RSI 36.4, and accelerating relative weakness vs SPY; need a close above 420 to reconsider.
Below both moving averages with -12% 4-week relative strength vs SPY and 17% drawdown; no sign of a base forming yet.
Sitting near its 200-day mean with RSI 40.3 after a sharp weekly drop; could bounce but relative strength is deteriorating—watching 165 as support.
Flat near its 50-day mean with middling RSI 47.7; outperforming mega-cap peers over 4 weeks but still -7.5% relative to SPY over 12 weeks.
Massive 26-week gain of +56% keeps it well above the 200-day mean, but 4-week relative weakness of -6.7% vs SPY suggests the trend is cooling; watching 300 as support.
Hovering right at its 200-day mean with RSI 43.2 and modest drawdown; not broken but not leading—needs to hold 290.
Down 51% from its 52-week high and 7% below the 200-day mean; despite a slight bounce this week, the structural damage is severe.

memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; UNH and XOM Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA and MSFT this quarter. NVDA's 10-K shows Q4 revenue of $68.13B (+73.2% YoY) with a staggering 63.1% net margin and net income nearly doubling at +94.5% YoY, all on minimal debt of $8.47B. MSFT posted $81.27B in revenue (+16.7% YoY) with net income surging 59.5% to $38.46B, driving a 47.3% net margin—margin expansion of this magnitude signals operating leverage kicking in across Azure and AI workloads. On the other side, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a razor-thin 2.1% net margin with $80.14B in debt, which is the kind of earnings compression I refuse to pay for until I see a clear inflection. XOM's revenue declined 1.3% with net income down 14.6% to $6.50B and a 7.9% net margin, reflecting commodity headwinds that may persist. GOOGL stands out as a strong compounder with 18% revenue growth and 30.3% net margins on a clean $14.79B debt load, while AMZN's 5.9% net income growth lags its 13.6% revenue growth, suggesting margin pressure I'd want to monitor.

views.note: 73% revenue growth, 63% net margin, near-doubling of net income, and only $8.47B debt make this the strongest earnings profile in the universe.
Net income up 59.5% YoY with a 47.3% net margin and moderate $40.26B debt signals durable, expanding earnings power from cloud and AI.
18% revenue growth, 30.3% net margin, and low $14.79B debt offer a compelling quality-growth combination; would reassess if ad revenue decelerates.
Revenue +15.7% and net income +15.9% with a 29.3% margin are solid, though $88.50B in total debt is the highest in the tech group and bears watching.
Revenue grew 13.6% but net income only 5.9%, compressing margins to 9.9%; I need to see operating leverage improve before getting constructive.
Revenue +7.1% is respectable for a bank but net income fell 7% YoY, suggesting provision or expense headwinds; 28.4% margin still decent but trajectory matters.
Revenue surged 18% but net income dropped 13.9%, indicating significant margin compression likely from input costs; need to see margin stabilization.
Only 1.5% revenue growth and a 6.7% decline in net income reflect a mature, low-growth profile; stable but not compelling at current multiples.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% net margin on $80.14B of debt—this is severe earnings compression and I won't pay for it until margins recover.
Revenue down 1.3% and net income down 14.6% with a thin 7.9% margin; commodity cyclicality is working against earnings durability right now.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Benign Inflation—Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Banks Over Defensives
memos.body: I see a clear mid-cycle easing regime: the fed funds upper bound is at 3.75%, down 75 bp over the past year, with the effective rate at 3.64% and CPI running at just 2.4% y/y—well-behaved enough to keep the Fed on a gradual cutting path. The unemployment rate at 4.30% has drifted up 30 bp y/y but ticked down 10 bp over three months, suggesting a softening but not deteriorating labor market. The 10y yield at 3.97% is down 32 bp y/y and the 2s10s curve has steepened to +60 bp, a positive signal for bank net interest margins and a tailwind for long-duration growth equities. I have conviction that this easing-plus-moderate-growth backdrop favors tech/growth and financials; a CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment spiking above 4.5% would force me to revisit the regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits directly from falling long rates and continued easing; 10y down 32 bp y/y supports multiple expansion.
Lower rates and stable consumer backdrop (unemployment only 4.3%) support premium consumer tech demand and valuation.
Easing cycle and falling long-end yields favor high-growth, long-duration names, though elevated valuation tempers confidence slightly.
Steepening 2s10s curve (+40 bp y/y to +60 bp) directly boosts NIM; easing cycle historically positive for bank credit quality.
Consumer spending resilient with moderate unemployment and falling rates reduce discount rates on its long-duration cash flows.
Staples lose relative appeal as easing favors cyclicals and growth; 2.4% CPI is manageable but doesn't provide pricing-power tailwind.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst in a moderate-growth, easing environment; no strong signal either way from current data.
Cyclical bellwether should benefit from easing but labor market softening y/y (+30 bp) tempers conviction on capex acceleration.
Ad-driven revenue benefits from stable consumer economy; lower discount rates support valuation of durable growth.
Defensive healthcare managed care is less rate-sensitive; macro backdrop neither strongly positive nor negative for the name.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: Defensive Names Holding Up While Big Tech and UNH Face Negative Tone Shifts
memos.body: I am reading a clear split in post-earnings sentiment across the universe this quarter. MSFT (-10.0%), NVDA (-5.5%), AMZN (-5.6%), and UNH (-19.6%) all saw sharp negative price reactions to their earnings 8-Ks, signaling genuine narrative deterioration rather than noise—these are large moves that suggest the market is repricing expectations lower. On the defensive side, PG (+2.6%), CAT (+3.4%), XOM (+0.6%), and AAPL (+0.5%) posted mildly positive or flat reactions, indicating stable-to-improving tone. JPM's -4.2% earnings-day drop in mid-January is now over six weeks old and likely priced, but the steady stream of subsequent 8-Ks (five filings since) suggests elevated corporate activity that warrants monitoring. I have highest conviction on avoiding UNH given the magnitude of the negative reaction and the subsequent executive departure filing on 2/25, which compounds the negative narrative.

views.note: A -19.6% earnings reaction followed by an executive departure 8-K on 2/25 signals a deeply negative and still-evolving narrative.
A -10.0% post-earnings drop is the largest negative reaction among mega-cap tech and suggests a meaningful sentiment reset that may not yet be fully digested.
The -5.5% reaction to the 2/25 earnings 8-K is very fresh (one day old) and negative sentiment is likely still building in media coverage.
A +2.6% earnings reaction and steady Reg FD disclosures point to a stable positive tone in a risk-off environment.
The +3.4% earnings pop and governance changes suggest constructive sentiment; industrial tone is holding up.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and routine shareholder vote filing suggest neither positive nor negative narrative momentum.
A -5.6% post-earnings drop on 2/6 indicates a negative tone shift that is still relatively recent.
The -4.2% earnings reaction is six weeks old and likely priced, but heavy 8-K filing activity keeps me from turning constructive.
Flat +0.6% earnings reaction and routine filings suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment.
A mild -0.5% earnings reaction is essentially noise; the subsequent 'Other Events' filing on 2/13 adds no clear directional signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 38% in Three Months While Oil Climbs—Geopolitical Risk Repricing Underway
memos.body: I am watching a sharp acceleration in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, now at 319 (+37.8% over three months and +10.2% in the last month alone), alongside a VIX that has risen 15.4% in a month to 18.63. WTI crude at $65.10 is up nearly 11% over three months, suggesting either supply-side tightening or geopolitical risk premia building in energy markets. High-yield spreads have widened modestly (+29 bps in a month to 2.98%) but remain historically tight, so credit markets are not yet pricing a severe shock—this tells me the uncertainty is policy-driven (tariffs, export controls, sanctions posturing) rather than a full-blown conflict scenario. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy China/export-control exposure (NVDA, AAPL) face asymmetric downside from further policy escalation, while domestically oriented or energy-levered names (XOM, JPM) are better positioned. A reversal in my view would require a clear de-escalation signal—e.g., a formal tariff rollback or export-control exemption announcement.

views.note: Structurally exposed to tightening semiconductor export controls toward China; elevated policy uncertainty index at 319 signals further restrictions are plausible.
Supply-chain concentration in China and rising policy uncertainty create headline risk; less direct than NVDA but still materially exposed.
WTI up 10.7% over three months to $65.10 amid geopolitical supply concerns; XOM's Reg FD filings suggest active investor communication around the energy outlook.
Domestically anchored revenue base, positive yield curve slope at 60 bps, and manageable HY spreads at 2.98% support the franchise; four 8-K filings in two months suggest proactive positioning.
Infrastructure spending tailwinds offset by tariff/input-cost risk from rising policy uncertainty; Reg FD filing in late January may have addressed guidance but details are unclear.
Defensive profile helps in elevated-uncertainty regimes, but FX headwinds and potential retaliatory tariffs on consumer goods keep me from going outright long.
